image_description: A close-up, high-angle shot of a male mallard duck (drake) swimming in clear, shallow water. The duck features a characteristic iridescent green head, a white neck ring, a yellow bill, and a brown/grey body. The water reveals submerged rocks below the surface.

checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The bill is clearly visible, broad, flat, and yellow-green in color, matching the description perfectly.
The eye is visible and appears dark/black, consistent with the taxonomy.

checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The body shape is compact and sits low in the water, indicating buoyancy. The plumage appears dense and smooth, repelling water effectively.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Breeding plumage is typically more colorful than female: common patterns include iridescent green head with white neck ring and grey body (mallard), or chestnut head with grey body.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The image displays the classic mallard drake pattern: iridescent green head, distinct white neck ring, and brownish-grey body feathers.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Legs are short and set far back on the body with webbed feet (three forward toes connected by webbing).
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The duck is swimming, and its legs/feet are submerged and completely occluded by the water and body angle. They cannot be visually verified.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Tail is short with curled central tail feathers (drake feathers) in many species.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The rear of the duck shows short tail feathers, and the characteristic upward curl of the central tail feathers (sexually dimorphic trait of drakes) is visible.
